commonPitfalls: Forgetting to set status=failed in the catch block of ProcessDocumentJob — documents can get stuck at status=processing indefinitely.
Not stopping the 5-second polling on /documents when all rows reach a terminal status — causes unnecessary backend load.
Using a plain text column for ocr_text without a tsvector/GIN index — full-text search becomes a sequential scan on large archives.
Omitting to concatenate JSONB values into the tsvector — searches miss hits that are only in extracted_fields.
Serving the uploaded file directly from the API without streaming or presigned URLs — blocks the Node process on large PDFs.
Not handling multi-page PDFs in the PaddleOCR sidecar — only the first page gets OCR'd unless pages are split before dispatch.
Confidence stored as FLOAT with no CHECK constraint — values outside 0-1 can break colour-coding chips silently.
Seed data with all documents in terminal status — the auto-refresh feature is invisible; ensure at least one row stays in status=processing at app start.
description: Internal admin tool for uploading paper/PDF records, running OCR via PaddleOCR sidecar and AI field extraction, and searching the resulting structured + full-text content.

designPatterns.description: After upload, the /documents table polls GET /api/documents every 5 s when hasProcessing is true. The API returns a top-level hasProcessing flag so the client can halt polling once all jobs are terminal, avoiding unnecessary requests.
designPatterns.name: Async Job Status Polling

designPatterns.description: POST /api/documents accepts multipart/form-data with multiple files, writes a Document row per file at status=queued, dispatches ProcessDocumentJob per document ID, and returns 202 Accepted with an array of document IDs.
designPatterns.name: Multipart Upload + Immediate Job Dispatch

designPatterns.description: PaddleOCR runs as a separate process or HTTP sidecar. The workflow calls it per-document (image or PDF page), receives raw text and per-character/region confidence scores, and aggregates a document-level confidence scalar (mean or min).
designPatterns.name: PaddleOCR Sidecar Integration

designPatterns.description: extracted_fields is stored as PostgreSQL JSONB. A GIN index on the column (jsonb_ops) allows containment queries. A generated tsvector column concatenates ocr_text with all JSONB string values for unified full-text search via a second GIN index.
designPatterns.name: JSONB Extracted Fields with GIN Index

designPatterns.description: Detail page splits horizontally: left panel shows the original file inline (PDF iframe or for images), right panel shows a DescriptionList of extracted key→value pairs, each with a colour-coded confidence Chip. A collapsible accordion below reveals raw OCR text in a monospace pre block.
designPatterns.name: Two-Column Document Viewer

designPatterns.description: Document status is rendered as a coloured Tag/Badge: queued=slate, processing=amber+spinner, complete=green, failed=red. Lets operators scan the table for actionable rows at a glance.
designPatterns.name: Coloured Status Tag

designPatterns.description: Search results surface a highlighted text snippet from ocr_text (using ts_headline in Postgres or client-side highlight). If the matching document has customer_name or account_number in extracted_fields, those are shown as prominent callout badges beside the filename.
designPatterns.name: Snippet Search with Field Callouts

designPatterns.description: Numeric confidence (0-1) is rendered as a small Chip: green (≥0.8), amber (0.5-0.79), red (<0.5). Applied both to individual extracted fields and as a document-level indicator in the table.
designPatterns.name: Confidence Chip Colour Coding

designPatterns.description: react-dropzone (or equivalent) multi-file dropzone shows each accepted file as a row with filename, size, and a pending/uploading/done chip. Upload button triggers batch POST. On success, navigate to /documents.
designPatterns.name: File Dropzone with Per-File Status

contexts: /search — full-text query across ocr_text + extracted_fields values
Auth page — email + password, redirect to /upload on success

personas.api_generator: You generate REST/RPC API endpoints for a document vault: POST /api/documents (multipart upload, dispatches ProcessDocumentJob per file), GET /api/documents (paginated, ordered by uploaded_at DESC), GET /api/documents/:id, GET /api/search?q= (full-text across ocr_text + extracted_fields values). Polling: the /api/documents response includes a hasProcessing boolean so the client knows whether to keep auto-refreshing. Return 202 on upload dispatch.
personas.auth_agent: Single role: Admin. Use session-based or JWT auth with a simple email+password login. No MFA required (internal tool). Protect all /api/* routes with a middleware guard that checks the session/token. No RBAC complexity needed — any authenticated user is an Admin.
personas.business_logic: You implement async document processing workflows: on upload, write Document with status=queued, then dispatch ProcessDocumentJob. The job calls the PaddleOCR sidecar (HTTP or subprocess), writes ocr_text + confidence, then calls the AI extraction step for [customer_name, account_number, amount, date, reference_number], merges results into extracted_fields JSONB, and does a final DB update to status=complete + processed_at=NOW(). On any step failure, catch and write status=failed + error_message. Never throw unhandled — always land in one terminal status.
personas.component_builder: You build React/TSX components for a document vault admin UI: FileDropzone (react-dropzone, multi-file, shows per-file status chips), DocumentsTable (TanStack Table, coloured status Tag, auto-refresh every 5 s while hasProcessing), DocumentViewer (two-column: PDF/image iframe left, DescriptionList of extracted_fields with confidence Chip right, collapsible OCR text panel below), SearchResults (snippet highlight, customer_name + account_number callout badges). Use a neutral dark-slate + electric-indigo colour scheme with monospace text for OCR output.
personas.contract_writer: You write TypeScript contracts (interfaces, enums, Zod schemas) for a document-vault domain. Key entities: Document (file, original_filename, uploaded_at, status enum [queued|processing|complete|failed], ocr_text, extracted_fields JSONB, confidence 0-1, error_message, org_id, processed_at). Workflow payload: ProcessDocumentJob { documentId }. Use domain language: OCR confidence, extracted fields, processing status.
personas.default: You are a senior full-stack engineer working on an internal document digitisation admin tool with OCR and AI field extraction. Prioritise correctness of async workflow state, accurate full-text search across JSONB, and a clean data-dense UI. Scope strictly to the described spec.
personas.design: Neutral, utilitarian admin aesthetic — dark slate backgrounds with electric indigo accents and warm amber status highlights. Typography is monospace-influenced for OCR/data fidelity, with a clean sans-serif for UI chrome. Density is compact to fit data-heavy document tables without scrolling fatigue.
personas.page_assembler: You assemble pages for a single-role admin tool. Three main pages: /upload (centred dropzone card, prominent Upload button, navigates to /documents on submit), /documents (full-width table with top-bar status legend and live refresh indicator), /documents/:id (two-column split viewer, breadcrumb back to /documents), /search (single SearchInput hero, results list below). Shell: fixed left sidebar with icons+labels for Upload, Documents, Search.
personas.planner: You are an expert product architect for internal document-intelligence admin tools. You understand async OCR pipelines (queue → sidecar → AI extract → DB write), polling-based status UIs, and single-role admin workflows. Keep every feature scoped to the described spec — no multi-tenancy, no batch rollups, no edit workflows.
personas.qa_tester: You write tests for a document vault. Critical paths: multi-file upload dispatches one job per file and redirects; status polling stops when no rows are processing; document viewer renders PDF inline and shows all extracted_fields; search returns snippets and highlights matching terms in ocr_text and extracted_fields values; failed documents show error_message clearly; confidence chips reflect numeric value with colour coding (green ≥0.8, amber 0.5-0.79, red <0.5).
personas.schema_designer: You design PostgreSQL schemas for OCR document vaults. The documents table carries a tsvector generated column over ocr_text concatenated with the JSONB values of extracted_fields for unified full-text search. Add a GIN index on the tsvector column and a separate GIN index on extracted_fields (jsonb_ops). Status is a PG enum. Index uploaded_at DESC for the default list sort.
personas.shell: Fixed left sidebar (240 px), icon + label nav items: Upload (cloud-arrow-up icon), Documents (document-text icon), Search (magnifying-glass icon). Top bar shows org name + logged-in user avatar. Main content area scrolls independently. Active nav item highlighted with indigo left-border accent.

uncertainAreas: Exact sidecar communication protocol for PaddleOCR (HTTP REST vs subprocess stdout) — spec says 'sidecar' but does not clarify; assuming HTTP.
Whether PDF preview uses an iframe (native browser PDF renderer) or a library like pdf.js — both are viable; choice affects bundle size.
Storage backend for uploaded files (local disk, S3, GCS) — not specified; assumed local or S3-compatible object storage.
Job queue implementation (BullMQ, pg-boss, simple DB polling) — not specified; any of these are compatible with the described workflow.
Whether confidence is document-level (single scalar) or per-field — spec implies both (a single confidence column on Document and per-field in extracted_fields); resolution needs confirmation.
Whether /search should support phrase queries or just keyword OR matching — Postgres tsvector defaults to OR; phrase search needs tsquery adjustments.

visualLanguage.paletteCharacter: dark slate utility with electric indigo accents and warm amber status highlights
